b1-revolucion-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What Is a Revolution?
b1-revolucion-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about a class on revolutions. Carlos asks what a coup is.
b1-revolucion-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what happens in a coup.
cues: Say who takes power in a coup
Say what usually does not change
b1-revolucion-01.target: En un golpe, los militares que toman el poder cambian al gobernante, pero la sociedad muchas veces sigue igual.
b1-revolucion-01.english: In a coup, the military who take power change the ruler, but society often stays the same.
b1-revolucion-01.canDo: I can say what a revolution is for historians.

b1-revolucion-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Land in Bolivia
b1-revolucion-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading about Bolivia in 1952, and Meg asks what happened with the land.
b1-revolucion-02.prompt: Tell Meg what Bolivia did after the revolution of 1952.
cues: Say that Bolivia made a land reform
Use a phrase for the cause
b1-revolucion-02.target: A raíz de la revolución de 1952, Bolivia hizo una reforma agraria.
b1-revolucion-02.english: As a result of the revolution of 1952, Bolivia carried out a land reform.
b1-revolucion-02.canDo: I can say why many peasants had no land.

b1-revolucion-03.title: Communicative Challenge: How the Students Protested
b1-revolucion-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are at a museum with a section on social movements, and Carlos asks what the students did.
b1-revolucion-03.prompt: Tell Carlos how the students protested.
b1-revolucion-03.target: Los estudiantes protestaban escribiendo periódicos y haciendo reuniones.
b1-revolucion-03.english: The students protested by writing newspapers and holding meetings.
b1-revolucion-03.canDo: I can name the groups that formed social movements.

b1-revolucion-04.title: Communicative Challenge: After the Revolution
b1-revolucion-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are talking about a documentary on new governments, and Meg asks what they had to do.
b1-revolucion-04.prompt: Tell Meg what the new governments had to do.
cues: Say what they had to organise
Say that they had to find money
b1-revolucion-04.target: Los nuevos gobiernos tuvieron que organizar el Estado y buscar dinero.
b1-revolucion-04.english: The new governments had to organise the state and find money.
b1-revolucion-04.canDo: I can say what the new governments had to do after a revolution.

b1-revolucion-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Do Revolutions Happen?
b1-revolucion-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about a book on revolutions, and Carlos asks what historians think.
b1-revolucion-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what some historians believe.
cues: Say what others do not believe
b1-revolucion-05.target: Algunos historiadores creen que la desigualdad es la causa principal, pero otros no creen que sea suficiente.
b1-revolucion-05.english: Some historians believe that inequality is the main cause, but others do not believe that it is enough.
b1-revolucion-05.canDo: I can say what some historians believe about the causes of revolutions.

b1-revolucion-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: What I Learned About Revolutions
b1-revolucion-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about a class on revolutions, and Carlos asks which countries had one in the twentieth century.
b1-revolucion-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos which countries had a revolution and when.
b1-revolucion-consolidation.target: Hubo revoluciones en México en 1910, en Bolivia en 1952, en Cuba en 1959 y en Nicaragua en 1979.
b1-revolucion-consolidation.english: There were revolutions in Mexico in 1910, in Bolivia in 1952, in Cuba in 1959 and in Nicaragua in 1979.
b1-revolucion-consolidation.canDo: I can say what a revolution is and name the revolutions of the twentieth century.
